About Me

I’ve spent more than seven years troubleshooting technical problems and over twelve years supporting customers, including U.S.-based teams. My work spans managed IT services, Microsoft 365, remote desktop environments, networking basics and high-volume support. It also showed me how much time technicians devote to turning conversations into accurate documentation.

That experience shapes my move into applied AI. I’m building in Python, studying through Harvard’s CS50P, and using the Anthropic Python SDK and Claude Sonnet 5.5 in a hands-on project. I evaluate outputs against synthetic scenarios and my own helpdesk judgment, paying attention to missed information, invented details and when a human needs to review an answer.

I want to help teams adopt useful AI workflows that solve everyday problems while keeping reliability and people at the center.

Projects

TicketScribe AI

Prototype · Evaluation in Progress

A Python-based AI workflow for turning helpdesk phone-call transcripts into structured ticket notes. The aim is to help Managed Service Provider (MSP) technicians document issues consistently and spend less time writing after each call.

1

Transcript

Start with a synthetic helpdesk conversation, with no real customer data.

2

Structured Notes

Use an AI model to extract key details and draft ticket-ready documentation.

3

Human Evaluation

Check the notes and priority reasoning for accuracy, omissions and invented facts.

What I'm Evaluating

I compare generated notes with an answer key informed by helpdesk judgment. My checks look for captured facts, unsupported claims, hallucinated details and whether the ticket priority makes sense. The current test set uses synthetic support calls.

Tools and Approach

I use Python and the Anthropic Python SDK with Claude Sonnet 5.5 to generate outputs. Claude's platform supports my development work, while ChatGPT provides an additional check alongside Python-based scoring and my own review.

Human Judgment Stays Central. This project is being tested for reliability; its generated notes and future suggestions are intended to assist technicians, not make autonomous support decisions.

Next Steps: Expand the evaluation set and explore technician-facing troubleshooting suggestions, including possible causes and areas to investigate.
